BY THE BOARD: 
By this Decision and Order, and in accordance with L. 2025, c. 145, the New Jersey Board of 
Public Utilities (“Board” or “BPU”) considers directing the State’s investor-owned electric, water, 
and wastewater companies (“Utilities”) to implement a “Summer Termination Program” (“STP”) 
that protects eligible residential customers from service discontinuance during the summer 
months. 

Agenda Date: 5/21/26 
Agenda Item: 7A 
2 

BACKGROUND AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY 

On September 24, 2025, Acting Governor Tahesha Way signed L. 2025, c. 145 into law (“Act”). 
The Act directs the Board to establish an STP for public utilities that provide electric, sewer, or 
water service.1 The Act directs the Board to promulgate rules and regulations to establish an STP 
that prohibits discontinuance of such services from June 15 through August 31 each year (“STP 
Period”), requires restoration of service without reconnection fees, and mandates that Utilities 
discuss deferred payment arrangements with participants in arrears. 

STAFF RECOMMENDATION 

Because a formal rulemaking proceeding establishing the terms of a permanent STP will not be 
complete before the 2026 summer months, to comply with the Act, Board Staff (“Staff”) 
recommends the Board implement a temporary STP, thereby requiring the Utilities to comply with 
the following requirements from June 15, 2026 through August 31, 2026:2 

1) A public utility shall not discontinue electric, sewer, or water service during the period of 
June 15 through August 31 to a residential customer deemed eligible for the STP. Eligible 
customers include any customer who meets one or more of the categorical eligibility criteria 
for the Board’s WTP, pursuant to the Board’s administrative rules at N.J.A.C. 14:3-3A.5. 
These eligible categories include: 

a. Recipients of benefits under the Lifeline Credit Program; 
b. Recipients of benefits under the Federal Home Energy Assistance Program 
(“HEAP”); 
c. Recipients of Temporary Assistance to Needy Families; 
d. Recipients of Federal Supplemental Security Income; 
e. Recipients of Pharmaceutical Assistance to the Aged and Disabled; 
f. Recipients of General Assistance benefits; 
g. Recipients of the Universal Service Fund; 
h. Applicants of the Low-Income Household Water Assistance Program or any other 
State, local, or utility program that provides assistance or discounted rates 
specifically to help eligible customers pay wastewater or water bills that may exist 
at that time; or 
i. 
Residential customers who are unable to pay their utility bills due to circumstances 
beyond their control which shall include, but not be limited to, unemployment, 
illness, medical expenses, recent death of an immediate family member, and any 
other circumstances which might cause financial hardship. These customers 
should be permitted to self-certify by directly contacting their Utility or the Board’s 
Division of Customer Assistance. 

2) A residential customer who is eligible for and seeks utility shutoff protections under the 
STP, and whose electric, sewer, or water service has been terminated for nonpayment 
prior to June 15, shall have their service restored by their Utility no later than June 15, and 
no reconnection fee shall be charged. 

1 Codified at N.J.S.A. 40A:5A-31 to -32 and N.J.S.A. 48:2-29.56b. 
2 Where not specified, the Utilities should follow the existing regulations regarding the Winter Termination 
Program (“WTP”), where applicable. 

Agenda Date: 5/21/26 
Agenda Item: 7A 
3 

3) Prior to restoring service to an STP customer, a Utility may verify that the residential 
customer continues to reside in or occupy the place of residence for which service was 
terminated for nonpayment. 

4) During the period of June 15 through August 31, each Utility shall discuss a deferred 
payment arrangement with its residential customers who participate in the STP and are in 
arrears. All STP customers shall make good-faith payments during the STP period, if they 
are able to do so. 

5) The Utility shall refer to the Board for resolution of all disputes regarding the appropriate 
amount of down payment. Until the Board has rendered a determination in such an 
instance, the Utility shall not unilaterally discontinue service during the STP Period. 

6) If a customer receives financial assistance, such as HEAP heating benefits, the customer 
shall forward all benefits to their electric, water, or wastewater utility. 

7) During the period June 15 through August 31, the Utilities shall promote the STP to 
residential customers in the forms including, but not limited to, email, the Utility’s website, 
billing inserts, and frequent social media posts. The Utilities will send STP factsheets to 
residential customers in danger of disconnection during the STP period. Each electric, 
water, and wastewater utility shall submit drafts of their proposed fact sheets to Staff no 
later than June 8, 2026, for approval for use during the upcoming STP Period. The 
Utilities shall have conditional approval to use their submitted fact sheets for 
implementation on June 15, subject to approval by Staff. 

8) During the STP Period, the Utilities shall not request a security deposit or an addition to an 
existing security deposit from a customer who is eligible for and seeks the protection of the 
STP. 

9) The STP requirements shall not apply to shutoffs of service to a residential customer who 
is eligible for utility shutoff protections under the STP due to a utility emergency. 

10) The Utilities may terminate service to a residential customer who is eligible for STP if the 
customer connects, disconnects, or otherwise tampers with the meters, pipes, wires, or 
conduits of the utility for the purpose of obtaining electric, water, and wastewater service 
without payment. No discontinuance shall occur until the customer has been afforded all 
reasonable due process considerations in accordance with all applicable law. 

DISCUSSION AND FINDINGS 

After careful review of the Act and the Board’s existing Winter Termination Program rules, the 
Board HEREBY FINDS that Staff’s recommended requirements for a temporary STP pending 
enactment of permanent STP rules are reasonable and in accordance with the law. 

The Board HEREBY FINDS that a proposed STP rulemaking will provide the public with the 
opportunity to comment on the STP program so that the STP rules can address any issues not 
specified in the Act or detailed herein.3 

3 Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 48:2-29.56b the Board shall establish a Summer Termination Program (“STP”). The 
Board, in a companion item on this agenda, is issuing a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking establishing a STP.
